artists.biography:
John Parr (born 18 November 1954) is an English musician, best known for his 1985 US No. 1 hit single "St. Elmo's Fire". Parr has sold 10 million albums worldwide.

Parr was born in Worksop, England. His first entrance into music was when he was 12 years old and formed a band with two fellow schoolmates named The Silence. The band had achieved some success. They eventually became professional and started to tour Europe.

perplexity.description:
John Parr's 1984 self-titled debut is a rock album that established the Scottish singer-songwriter as a commercial force in the mid-1980s. The record showcases a polished rock sound with strong melodic sensibilities, featuring three Billboard Hot 100 entries that demonstrated its broad appeal across mainstream and rock radio formats. The album's most successful single, "Naughty Naughty," peaked at number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and reached the top 10 on the Mainstream Rock Chart, establishing Parr as a viable rock artist in the United States.

The album achieved wider international prominence following the 1985 UK reissue on London Records, which added "St. Elmo's Fire (Man in Motion)," the theme song for Joel Schumacher's film of the same name. This addition proved transformative for Parr's career; the track became a global phenomenon, reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100 for two weeks and earning a Grammy nomination, while also achieving number six status in his native UK. The inclusion of this track on subsequent versions of the album cemented its legacy as more than a debut effort—it became the vehicle for one of the decade's most recognizable rock anthems.
